headline: On November 11, 1992: Church of England votes to ordain women priests
captionCards: General Synod instituted in 1970, replacing Church Assembly

instagramCaption:
Women priests in the Church of England? It happened. 

On November 11, 1992, the General Synod of the Church of England voted to allow women to become priests. The synod, established in 1970, replaced the Church Assembly and is the church’s legislative body. A surprising detail: this decision followed decades of efforts toward self-government that began in the 1850s. 

The vote marked a pivotal shift in the church’s structure and inclusivity.
